title: Continue mapping Townscaper's full feature set (platforms/camera modes, color-as-generation-input mechanism, UX gaps) for future VTT structuring
objective: Owner-directed: continue capturing every Townscaper detail relevant to VTT integration so future architecture work covers these points. Researched via WebSearch/WebFetch (Wikipedia, UploadVR, a Steam Community palette-sharing guide, the latunda/townscaper GitHub repo) to confirm: (1) Townscaper shipped a VR mode (Meta Quest + Pico, October 2023) -- a real, successful precedent for the owner's just-decided free-camera requirement; (2) exact camera controls are player-driven rotate/zoom/time-of-day, not an automated day-night cycle; (3) the concrete technical spec of the 16-color/type palette system (a literal 1x16-pixel palette image) and the finding that color/type is itself a generation input, not just cosmetic (adjacent same-type blocks merge, alternating types at boundaries trigger different architectural rules such as doors/lighthouses vs. more windows/arches) -- directly precedents this project's own 'grid/parameter layer configures generation' idea; (4) no traditional undo/redo is documented in Townscaper itself, a real UX gap in the reference that this project's own Command/DomainEvent engine already closes for free, worth recording as a place to exceed the reference rather than just copy it; (5) checked latunda/townscaper on GitHub specifically to rule out whether an open-source Townscaper engine clone exists as a possible shortcut -- confirmed it is only a community palette/world-asset resource repository, not an engine reimplementation, so no such shortcut exists.
validations: Added a 'Platforms and camera modes' note recording Townscaper VR (Meta Quest/Pico, Oct 2023) as a shipped precedent for free-camera navigation, and that time-of-day/lighting is an explicit manual player control rather than an automated cycle.

Added a concrete 'Color/type as a generation input' subsection: the 16-color palette (1x16-pixel image format), the finding that adjacent same-type blocks merge while alternating types at boundaries trigger different architectural outcomes -- i.e. color/type is itself part of the constraint system, directly precedenting this document's own guided-construction-mode parameter-layer idea.

Recorded the absence of traditional undo/redo in Townscaper itself as a real UX gap, noting this repository's own Command/DomainEvent engine already provides it for free across every construction tier -- a place this project can exceed the reference model, not just copy it.

Recorded that latunda/townscaper (GitHub) was checked and ruled out as a potential open-source Townscaper-engine shortcut -- confirmed to be a community palette/world-asset repository only, not a reimplementation; no open-source Townscaper engine clone was found to exist.
No dependency installed, no code written -- documentation research/consolidation only.
risks: Web research reflects sources found today (2026-08-01) and may drift, per this document's existing dated-facts caveat.
